contract.direct_answer:
The evidence bundle does not contain the specific transcription-factor expression data needed to answer this question confidently. The retrieval returns only metadata/descriptions of resources (ZFIN, ZESTA/CORPUS-2026-0001, the RN1 lineage niche, CNGB STOmics) plus one on-topic chunk (CORPUS-2026-0003#c000) that merely states the zebrafish pronephros is a good in vivo system for studying nephron development — it does not enumerate markers, ENSDARG IDs, or temporal expression order.

What can be said from canonical pronephros biology is NOT supported by this bundle, so I will not assert it as fact. In general terms, intermediate mesoderm (the broader field that gives rise to kidney) is typically marked early by pax genes and lhx1/osr transcription factors, while pronephric/nephron segment identity is refined later by more restricted regulators; the temporal sequence (broad IM field → committed pronephric mesoderm → segmented nephron) is what constrains lineage, with early broad-domain TFs preceding and delimiting later segment-specific TFs. However, the bundle provides NO gene symbols, NO ENSDARG identifiers, and NO stage-resolved expression values to substantiate which specific TFs mark each compartment at 12–24 hpf or their exact expression order.

To answer properly I would need the per-cell-type / per-stage expression tables from ZESTA (CORPUS-2026-0001) or the RN1 lineage niche (transition-probability matrices + average expression per cell type), and verified ENSDARG bindings from ZFIN — none of which are present as actual data values in this bundle.
alternatives_considered: Assert canonical IM markers (pax2a, pax8, lhx1a, osr1/osr2) vs. pronephric segment TFs from memory — REJECTED because no ENSDARG or expression evidence is in the bundle and asserting gene IDs from memory violates the substrate contract.
Query ZESTA/RN1 expression tables directly for stage-resolved TF expression — the resources are indexed but their actual expression values are not in this bundle, so this cannot be executed here.
Treat the RN1 transition-probability matrices as evidence of lineage order — REJECTED because only the niche description, not the matrix contents, is provided.
